en: Mount Mayon in Albay has a nearly perfect conical shape formed by layers of solidified lava and volcanic ash.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea contains pristine coral atolls visible from the surface during low tide.
The giant Rafflesia flower, found in Philippine rainforests, blooms with five thick, reddish-brown petals.
The Philippine tarsier, active at night in Bohol's forests, uses its enormous eyes to hunt small insects.
Mount Pulag in Benguet is frequently covered by a sea of clouds observable above its 2,928-meter peak.
During the amihan season, the northeast monsoon brings clear skies and cool breezes to most of the Philippines.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao are carved into the mountainsides, creating visible, stepped irrigation ponds.
The Enchanted River in Surigao del Sur features crystal-clear, deep blue freshwater flowing from an underwater cave.
The Sierra Madre mountain range features dense, green tropical forests stretching along the eastern coast of Luzon.
Callao Cave in Peñablanca, Cagayan, contains large limestone chambers with natural skylights that let sunlight shine inside.
